edits.find: - **Just landed.** Slice D, `edit(recipe)`, and the hook derivation it earned.
edits.replace:
- **Just landed.** Slice E, one authored property inside a plugin group the node already authors. `setKeyframe(plugin, key, value)` and `removeKeyframe(plugin, key)` are the value tier narrowed to one leaf: both answer with the `PatchBatch` of one invalidate and neither reaches `replaceGraph` on any path, accepting or refusing, because a leaf carries no edge and a bound group's plugin is in the chain already. Two paths behind one verb, decided by the record rather than by the name: a key the group already authors is `setValues({ [key]: value })` with the group named, so `Track` keeps its per-key refusal ordering; a key it does not author yet cannot be masked at all, so the authored record is edited, the candidate is validated and resolved, and the node is recompiled in place and re-seeked to the progress it had. `domain/authoring/keyframes.ts` gains the two pure editors and `withValues`, the values-section twin of `withRequires` reaching the same `removeGroup`; `#boundGroup` becomes the one owner of the precondition all eight authored verbs share and `withKeyframes` the one owner of what an authored edit leaves behind on a `TrackDefinition`. `RA-69` through `RA-76` are its evidence and [ADR-065](./ADR-065-authored-property-editing.md) records the decisions it turned on.
- **The decision worth carrying forward from it.** A verb that rewrites the authored record is not thereby allowed to change what a key is. `setKeyframe` could have compiled a static key into an animated one rather than refusing the crossing, and refusing is the honest answer: two authored shapes for one key is a whole-definition question, `replace()` is where a whole definition is validated, and `Track` already owns the per-key refusal, so compiling it would have added a second authored shape and a second owner of leaf kind in one move. `RA-74` asserts both directions, because a refusal in one direction is not a rule.
- **The second one, about what a precondition is worth.** `keyframe-group-unbound` was read as honesty about which tier a caller is in, and it turns out to be what makes the cheap tier provable rather than asserted. A bound group's plugin is already resolved into the chain, because the registry pushes a named plugin in whether or not that group authors any values, so a leaf added to a bound group cannot add a composer or move one. A precondition that only refuses is documentation; this one buys the price.
- **Landed just before it.** Slice D, `edit(recipe)`, and the hook derivation it earned.

The leaf-kind crossing stays refused in both directions, `keyframe-key-animated` does not exist, and a plugin this node authors no group for is still `setKeyframeGroup`'s job. edits.find: - A gate reads code, never prose. A scan for a retired form is narrowed to what that form can be written in; product text is not reworded to satisfy an assertion.
edits.replace:
- A gate reads code, never prose. A scan for a retired form is narrowed to what that form can be written in; product text is not reworded to satisfy an assertion.
- A mechanical edit is read for the prose it moved as well as for the code. E's extraction of `#boundGroup` inserted it between `#editRequire` and the docblock that documents `#editRequire`'s order, which left one comment owning the wrong member and the new member owning none. A docblock is part of the thing it sits above, so a script that moves a member moves that too or leaves the member where it is, and the review reads the boundaries of the move rather than the diff of the body.
- A debt list is a measurement, not a ledger. The guide-debt list in this file was appended to per slice and never re-read, so four of its seven claims described work a later slice had already done, and a reader trusting it would have rewritten documentation that was already correct. It is rewritten from the files rather than from itself.

edits.replace:
`setKeyframe(plugin, key, value)` and `removeKeyframe(plugin, key)` are the same tier narrowed to one property of a plugin group this node already authors. Both answer with the `PatchBatch` of one invalidation and neither replaces the graph, on any path, because a leaf carries no edge and a bound group's plugin is in the chain already. Which of two paths a call takes is decided by the record rather than by the name: a key the group already authors is `setValues` with the group named, and a key it does not author yet is validated, resolved and compiled in place at the same progress, because a mask cannot express a key nothing compiled. The refusals are `keyframe-group-unbound` for a plugin this node authors no group for, which is `setKeyframeGroup`'s job, `LiveValueKeyError` with the `kind` reason for a leaf-kind crossing, which stays refused even though this verb rewrites the authored record, and whatever the plugin registry answers about a leaf the named group claims nothing about. There is no refusal for an animated key. Removing a group's last leaf removes the section, and a group left naming no section loses its entry. See ADR-065.

`edit(recipe)` on `ProjectHandle` runs `n` authored ops across `m` tracks as one transaction: one candidate build, one graph replacement, one `ObservationState` commit and one flush. The recipe is handed a `SchemaTransaction`, which carries `addMotion`, `motion`, `tryMotion`, `addTrack`, `track` and `tryTrack` and nothing else, so `mount`, `seek`, `subscribe` and `dispose` are not reachable through it. Reads inside the recipe resolve against what it has staged, so a two-step edit sees its own first step, and a throw commits nothing: no hook is reached and a handle issued inside the recipe never becomes live. A recipe inside a recipe is `schema-transaction-nested`, and a verb that applies immediately rather than committing is `schema-transaction-immediate`, named at the verb. See ADR-064.

edits.find: ## Changing values without rebuilding the graph
## A stale handle refuses, and `live` asks without throwing
edits.replace:
## One property of a group, without naming the rest

`overrideValues` and `setValues` take a record and answer for the whole node. To move one leaf of one plugin group, name the group:

```ts
track.setKeyframe("fk", "length", 12);
track.setKeyframe("fk", "rotation", [
  { p: 0, v: 0 },
  { p: 1, v: 45 },
]);
track.removeKeyframe("fk", "length");
```

Both are the value tier, so both return the `PatchBatch` of their one invalidation and neither rebuilds the graph, on any path. That holds because a leaf carries no edge and the plugin it belongs to is already in the chain: this pair only edits a group the node already authors, and `keyframe-group-unbound` is what you get for naming a plugin it does not. Originating a group is still `setKeyframeGroup`'s job, because a group holding only half its data may be transiently invalid.

A key the group already authors takes the path `setValues` takes, with the same per-key refusals in the same order. A key it does not author yet cannot be masked, because nothing compiled it, so the authored record is edited and the node is recompiled in place and re-seeked to the progress it had. That new leaf is the one thing this pair can do that the record-shaped members cannot.

The leaf-kind crossing is still refused, and that is a decision rather than an unfinished edge. This verb rewrites the authored record, so it could have compiled a scalar over an animated key, and it does not: which kind of leaf a key is authored as is a whole-definition question that `replace()` owns. An animated key itself is fine, exactly as it is through `setValues`.

`removeKeyframe` takes the empty shapes with it. The values section goes when its last leaf does, the group goes when it names no section, and the definition loses its `keyframes` key when it holds nothing, so dropping the only leaf of a group that binds nothing removes the group and the plugin leaves the chain with it. That is what an author writing the same document would have written. A key the group does not author is a no-op. See ADR-065.

## A stale handle refuses, and `live` asks without throwing

edits.find: - a disposed clock or trigger port throws when subscribed to.
edits.replace:
- `handle.edit(recipe)` refuses two things by name, and both are about where a call was made. A recipe opened inside a recipe throws with `schema-transaction-nested`, because one transaction is the unit and nesting would give it two. A verb that applies immediately throws with `schema-transaction-immediate`, named at the verb so the message tells you which call to move out: `setTrigger` and `setStagger` on a `MotionHandle`, and `overrideValues`, `setValues`, `setKeyframe` and `removeKeyframe` on a `TrackHandle`. A settle step cannot refuse, so deferring one of those into the transaction would move its failure to after the graph had committed and the retained definition had moved, and one condition would end up with two failure contracts. A throw from inside the recipe commits nothing and leaves every handle it issued not live. See ADR-064.
- a disposed clock or trigger port throws when subscribed to.
